name: Jellyfin Federation
overview: Allows jellyfin servers to federate with each other
description: This Jellyfin plugin allows multiple Jellyfin servers to federate, sharing media libraries in real-time without syncing or copying files. Media can be streamed from one server to another with live transcoding if necessary.

versions.changelog:
Fixed the real cause of federated playback taking minutes to start: on a server reached through a public reverse proxy, VPS, or tunnel (the normal setup for most installs), a Proxy-mode stream's URL pointed at that public hostname - so this server's own transcoder round-tripped every byte of the source file back out through DNS/the tunnel just to reach itself. This hit every server with a ServerUrl configured, which peer handshakes require - effectively everyone running Proxy mode. Proxy-mode stream URLs now always resolve to loopback (127.0.0.1) instead, for both the primary source and any alternate multi-server sources, since they are only ever fetched by the local ffmpeg process and never by a client directly. The previous 0.0.64 fix (AnalyzeDurationMs on the federated MediaSourceInfo, intended to shrink ffmpeg's probe) has been removed - live logs confirmed it had no effect on the actual ffmpeg invocation in this Jellyfin version.

Recolored the corner "federated source" badge on grid/list cards from a theme-accent-colored circle to a neutral dark chip. The accent color made it visually indistinguishable from Jellyfin's own theme-accent played-checkmark badge; the dark chip stays legible over any poster art without being mistaken for a native state badge.

198 tests.

Fixed federated playback taking minutes to start. Jellyfin defaulted -analyzeduration 200M / -probesize 1G on the HTTP proxy stream, so ffmpeg pulled hundreds of megabytes through the tunnel before it would begin writing HLS segments even though the remote already told us every stream in the file. Setting AnalyzeDurationMs on the federated MediaSourceInfo drops that to a bounded probe when we have authoritative stream info in hand, cutting click-to-first-frame from minutes to seconds. Playback itself was already fine once started - only startup is affected.

Redesigned the federated-item badges. The cloud glyph is now filled instead of an outline-with-up-arrow (which read like an upload icon), the source/download/hide chips size in real pixels instead of at .5em relative to the H1 title (which came out as tiny cramped ovals hanging off the page), and they now use the active Jellyfin theme accent color and typographic scale so they read as part of the page instead of pasted onto it. Adds a light-theme override so the outlined chip does not disappear on a white background.

198 tests (unchanged).

Removed the floating download-progress toast that appeared at the bottom of the screen on every page - it read as this plugin editing jellyfin-web's own chrome, which wasn't the goal. Download progress is still visible everywhere it matters: the pill next to the title and the progress ring drawn on the cover art (both on the item's own page), and the Downloads section on the Federation settings page.

198 tests (unchanged).

Redesigned the settings page's visual style: a consistent spacing/color/radius system now underlies every card, status pill, and alert banner instead of one-off values accumulated across many releases, and the four sections used most often - status, Downloads, Add a friend, and People - now visually stand out from the rarely-touched advanced/diagnostic sections. Collapsed sections got a proper disclosure-triangle indicator, focus states were added to the page's own custom interactive elements (Select all/Clear, collapsible section headers, checkbox rows), and layout now compresses gracefully in a narrower browser window instead of using fixed spacing. Purely visual - no endpoint, field, or behavior changed.

198 tests (unchanged).

Backfills last release's MediaStreams fix onto items that already existed before it: previously only newly-synced items got real codec/resolution/audio data saved (existing items only ever had their stream URL and duration refreshed, not this), so anything already in your library would have kept probing/transcoding until it happened to be deleted and recreated. Reconciliation now does a one-time backfill for any federated item that doesn't have stream data yet - no full resync or re-add needed, it self-heals on the next scheduled sync.

198 tests (unchanged).

Fixed the real cause of federated playback taking a long time to start. The remote's real per-stream data (video/audio codecs, resolution, channels) was never being saved on the local item - only the container - so Jellyfin's own compatibility check had nothing to compare against and fell back to a live probe through the proxy on every single play before anything could start, then very often transcoded even when the file would have played back directly. The sync now requests and saves the remote's real stream data (already available in the same response, no extra network calls needed), so Jellyfin can certify direct play immediately in the common case instead of probing over the WAN link first. Confirmed against this server's own logs: previously every federated title was being remuxed through ffmpeg before playback could begin, including files whose video and audio were already fully compatible.

The Downloads section now also shows the destination file path and an estimated time remaining for each active download, alongside the existing size/speed/progress bar.

198 tests (up from 196).

Fixed the settings page (and the client badge script) potentially serving a stale cached copy after an upgrade: both were served with no caching headers at all, which left it up to each browser's own heuristics whether a revisit re-fetched them or served a stale cached copy - a real, previously-hit source of "I shipped a fix but it doesn't look like it's there" (see WebClientInjector's own permission-bug history this session). Both now send an explicit no-store, so an update is always visible on the next page load. This is very likely why the Downloads section added last release wasn't showing up for some admins even though the feature itself was working.

The Downloads section's progress bar now uses the active theme's own accent color (falling back to Jellyfin's default teal if a theme doesn't define one) instead of a fixed color, so it matches whatever theme is selected rather than always looking the same regardless of it.

196 tests (unchanged).

Added a Downloads section to the Federation settings page: every download in progress (or recently finished) shows its progress bar, transfer speed, and a Cancel button, in one place instead of only being visible on the item's own detail page.

Added a circular progress ring drawn right over an item's cover art while it's downloading - on the poster in library grids, search results, and home rows, and on the detail page's own cover image - since the item already has its real artwork synced from the friend's server, this just overlays progress on what's already there. Updates live wherever that cover art currently appears, not just on the page you started the download from.

Download speed is now tracked and shown everywhere progress is shown (the pill, the toast, the new dashboard section, and the ring's percentage) - computed from actual bytes transferred, sampled about once a second so it reads as a stable number instead of jumping around.

196 tests (unchanged - this release is UI/progress-reporting work, the download mechanism itself is unchanged: still a direct authenticated HTTP transfer from the friend's server to yours).

Added the ability to cancel a download in progress: click the "Download to server" pill again while it's downloading (it now shows a percentage and "click to cancel") to stop it - the partially-written file is deleted and the connection to the friend's server is closed immediately, rather than letting it run to completion in the background with no way to stop it. This also fixes a real gap: the download job previously ignored its cancellation token entirely, so there was no way to interrupt one even server-side.

A failed or cancelled download now leaves the pill clickable again right away (labeled "Failed - retry?") instead of stuck in a dead-end state, so retrying doesn't require leaving and reopening the item's page.

Also, for anyone wondering: downloads already go directly from your friend's server to yours over a plain authenticated HTTP request - no relay, no third party, no cloud service in between. This release doesn't change that, just adds a way to stop one partway through.

196 tests (up from 194).

Reverted last release's attempt to move "Download to server" into jellyfin-web's own "more actions" (⋮) menu - cloning into that live popup ended up removing the rest of its options (Edit metadata, Edit images, Identify, etc.) for some users, which is a much worse outcome than a pill that just looked a little crowded. The native menu is untouched again.

Removed the floating "Origin filter" control entirely, per feedback that it wasn't wanted.

Download to server is back as its own pill next to Streamed-from/Hide, but redesigned to stop colliding with the title: it now renders on its own row directly below the title instead of jammed inline before it, so a stylized show-logo title has room and the pills read as a small action bar underneath rather than fighting the title for space.

Fixed download progress disappearing on refresh: the in-progress state is now saved (which item, which operation) so reloading the page - or coming back to the item later - resumes polling and restores the pill/toast instead of leaving no indication a download was ever running.

194 tests (unchanged - this release is client-script only, no server-side logic changed).

Fixed the client-side badge script (Web/federation-badge.js): a stray pair of literal NUL bytes had crept into the origin-filter code, which is harmless to the browser but corrupts anything expecting normal text - fixed by using a proper \u0000 escape instead. Also fixed a real display bug: the Download/Hide pills' progress text was being written into the wrong inner element (their icon, not their label), which is why the download pill visibly garbled itself mid-download instead of showing a percentage cleanly.

Moved "Download to server" out of a standalone pill next to the title - it was fighting a stylized show-logo title for space and looked broken - into jellyfin-web's own "more actions" (⋮) menu, alongside Edit metadata/Refresh metadata/etc., with progress now shown as a small toast instead. It's cloned from a real menu item already in that menu (icon and label swapped) rather than styled from scratch, so it automatically matches whatever theme is active.

Made the floating origin-filter control and the download-progress toast theme-adaptive: they now pull their colors from the active theme's own CSS variables (falling back to the previous dark palette if a theme doesn't define them), so a custom theme's colors carry through instead of a fixed dark chip regardless of theme. The corner badge and title/hide pills stay a fixed solid color on purpose - they sit over poster art and backdrop images, not page background, the same reasoning behind Jellyfin's own always-dark played-checkmark badge.

Also fixed the badge/download/hide scripts never actually running on this install: jellyfin-web's index.html was owned by root while the server process runs as a regular user, so the plugin's every attempt to inject its client script into the page failed silently on every startup - permission fixed, script now injects and loads correctly.

194 tests (unchanged - this release is client-script and deployment fixes, no server-side logic changed).

Rebuilt the Federation settings page from scratch around one simple flow instead of two confusing ones. Adding a friend used to mean either a clean URL-only handshake or an older path where you had to copy an API key by hand from the other server's Dashboard - the key-paste path and its "Remote user" dropdown are gone; there's just one "type their server address" flow now, and the account used to pull a friend's library is resolved automatically the same way playback already did. Per-friend sharing (what a friend can see of your library) and pools are promoted out of a stack of buried, nested disclosures into a real "People" panel per friend.

Added "download to server": on a federated item's detail page, a Download button fetches the file from the friend's server and saves it locally, so it plays back afterward with no dependency on their server being online - it becomes a completely ordinary local item once the next library scan picks it up. Also added a way to add an already-connected friend straight into a pool (no re-typing their address).

Added an origin filter for library grids and search results: a small floating "Origin filter" control (reusing the same data the corner/pill badges already fetch) lists local content plus every friend server seen so far, each with a checkbox - uncheck a server to hide its items from the current view, or uncheck everything except one to see only that server's content. The choice is remembered across navigation via localStorage. It's a standalone control rather than a hook into jellyfin-web's native filter dialog, since that dialog's internal markup isn't something this plugin can safely target from outside a jellyfin-web fork.

Added a local "Hide" action for federated items: on a federated item's detail page, a Hide button (next to Download) removes it from your own library browsing/search/home going forward - useful for a friend's low-quality rip of something you already own in better quality, or content you just don't want cluttering your library. This is purely local: the friend is never notified and keeps sharing normally, and it's unrelated to per-friend sharing permissions (which control what a friend can see of *your* content, the opposite direction). Manage and unhide previously-hidden items from a new "Hidden items" section on the settings page; an unhidden item reappears on the next sync.

Added per-remote-user access overrides: the People panel for each friend now lists that friend's own local user accounts (fetched live from their server), and clicking one lets you block them entirely, narrow them to a subset of the libraries already shared with that friend, or narrow them all the way down to specific items - layered on top of the existing per-friend sharing scope, never widening it. Since a friend's whole server queries under one shared account today, there was no way for a friend's admin to distinguish which of their own users was asking; the rule you set is now pushed to the friend's own plugin, which enforces it locally against whichever of their users is actually browsing or streaming, re-checked again at the moment a Proxy-mode stream is requested. No rule configured (the common case) behaves exactly as before. Item-level picking reuses a new minimal local item search endpoint since none existed on this page yet.

Fixed federated items being invisible to Jellyfin's own Continue Watching, Latest, and library-browsing queries even though playback itself worked fine. Root cause: federated items have no real file behind them (their Path is a URL on the friend's server), so their library's on-disk shadow folder is always genuinely empty - and Jellyfin's own library scan refuses to register a physical Folder for an empty folder, skipping it as "inaccessible or empty" instead. Without that physical Folder, federated items ended up parented directly to the library itself, and every query Jellyfin runs by ancestor/top-parent (Continue Watching, Latest, Recommended, browsing the library, any Home screen widget) resolves that parent to zero physical folders and comes back empty - confirmed against a live server: the item was always still reachable by its own id (direct fetch, PlaybackInfo, the Sessions/Now Playing panel while actively playing), just invisible to anything that lists by library. A hidden marker file dropped into each federation library's shadow folder keeps it non-empty, so Jellyfin registers a real physical Folder for it exactly like any other library, and federated items become visible everywhere a local item would be, including their resume position after playback stops. Existing installations self-heal on upgrade: provisioning now also backfills the marker into already-created shadow folders and prompts a library scan so previously-affected items are picked up without waiting on the next scheduled one.

194 tests (up from 192).

Rebuilt the Federation settings page from scratch around one simple flow instead of two confusing ones. Adding a friend used to mean either a clean URL-only handshake or an older path where you had to copy an API key by hand from the other server's Dashboard - the key-paste path and its "Remote user" dropdown are gone; there's just one "type their server address" flow now, and the account used to pull a friend's library is resolved automatically the same way playback already did. Per-friend sharing (what a friend can see of your library) and pools are promoted out of a stack of buried, nested disclosures into a real "People" panel per friend.

Added "download to server": on a federated item's detail page, a Download button fetches the file from the friend's server and saves it locally, so it plays back afterward with no dependency on their server being online - it becomes a completely ordinary local item once the next library scan picks it up. Also added a way to add an already-connected friend straight into a pool (no re-typing their address).

173 tests (up from 164).

Fixed the real cause of "federated playback takes minutes to start, then stutters every ~20 seconds": Proxy-mode streaming already commits a Content-Length header covering the whole remaining file, and video players constantly open and cancel range requests as completely normal behavior (seeking, prefetching, probing). The server was treating each of those ordinary cancellations as a successful response and just returning - which left the underlying ASP.NET server to discover far fewer bytes were actually written than promised and forcibly reset the TCP connection instead of closing it cleanly. Players see a reset very differently from an ordinary closed connection: it looked like a hard streaming error on nearly every single range request, forcing expensive recovery (re-fetching playback info, rebuilding the media source) instead of just opening the next request. The connection is now aborted deliberately instead, so an ordinary cancelled request no longer looks like a crash.

Three more bugs found and fixed alongside it: a stream retry from a resumed offset now requires the remote to actually answer with a matching partial-content response, instead of accepting a plain 200-from-the-start answer and splicing it onto bytes already sent to the client (this was corrupting playback rather than just stalling it, for any remote/proxy that dropped the Range header on a retried request); an auto-resolved playback user was getting silently written into the saved server configuration and persisted to disk by any unrelated save, instead of staying in memory for the session; and an episode whose series wasn't synced yet was being created as a loose, disconnected item at the library root instead of being skipped and retried on a later sync.

164 tests (up from 161), including regression coverage that reproduces each of these against the pre-fix code.

Per-friend sharing controls, and two real bugs found while building them.

Added per-friend library sharing: pick which of this server's own libraries a specific friend can see, defaulting to everything (unchanged from before). Enforced through Jellyfin's own EnabledFolders account policy rather than anything this plugin polices itself - the same mechanism used to restrict a family member's login. The admin picks an existing local Jellyfin user for this rather than the plugin creating one automatically: IUserManager.CreateUserAsync does not work reliably on every server build - it can leave a new user's AuthenticationProviderId unset and then fail its own save with a NOT NULL constraint, before ever handing the created user back to plugin code to fix up, since the failure happens inside Jellyfin's own creation path. Reusing an account Jellyfin's admin UI already created successfully sidesteps the bug entirely, and is arguably better anyway - the account is fully visible and manageable from the normal Dashboard, not a hidden one this plugin invents. Also found and fixed: listing local Jellyfin users threw MissingMethodException on at least one real server build, because the member exposing it changed shape (a `Users` property in the NuGet package this plugin compiles against, a `GetUsers()` method on the actual running server) - now read through reflection so it works against either shape instead of binding to whichever one happened to be present at compile time.

Pools got two fixes. First, adding a friend you already have to a pool used to fail outright ("already friends") because it went through the same handshake used for a genuinely new contact - defeating the entire point of a pool, which is not repeating that handshake for people you're already connected to. Adding an existing friend now just adds them to the pool locally and sends them a notice, no accept step needed since the two servers already trust each other; only a real stranger goes through the full friend-request flow. Second, the notice this sends (and the sharing-update notice from the paragraph above) was never actually being received on the other end - the request carried no API key, so the friend's server would have rejected it outright as unauthorized. Neither had ever been exercised against a live peer before now, so this had gone unnoticed. Multiple pools already worked correctly; nothing was blocking that.

Also fixed a CSS bug in last release's own black-text fix: it forced light text using an ID selector, which outranks Jellyfin's own button/element styling by CSS specificity and could make some things - like a light-background button expecting dark text - illegible in the other direction. Rewritten with :where() so it only fills in a color where nothing else set one, and never overrides an element's own deliberate styling.

160 tests (up from 150), including coverage for the existing-friend pool fast path, the pool notice fan-out, and the sharing feature's rejection paths.

A large batch fixing three separate causes of "everything is duplicated," the seeking/playback-stall bug, and a wrong-duration bug, plus multi-server pools.

Duplicates had two independent root causes. First, PruneServerSources only detected a stale cache entry being superseded by a newer key in the raw-to-provider direction (an item first cached without provider ids, then re-keyed once dedup matched it) - the far more common reverse direction, a provider-keyed entry losing its claim to a raw or different-provider key, was never checked, so the old copy survived forever. Second, and more fundamentally: dedup compares provider ids using the lowercase names in DedupProviderIds ("imdb", "tmdb", "tvdb"), but Jellyfin stamps them Pascal-cased ("Imdb", "Tmdb") on both BaseItem and BaseItemDto, and neither dictionary is guaranteed case-insensitive. A plain TryGetValue("imdb", ...) against a dictionary keyed "Imdb" silently missed every real entry - in three separate places (cross-server dedup, and both directions of "don't federate what's already owned locally"). Dedup had never actually matched anything, ever, regardless of the EnableDedup toggle. Both are fixed: PruneServerSources now checks supersession symmetrically for raw and provider-keyed entries, and a new case-insensitive FederationLibraryManager.TryGetProviderId replaces every raw TryGetValue call. Verified live: 311 stale Movie entries and 27 Shows entries pruned on the first sync after the cache fix; after also fixing the case bug and turning dedup on, a further 30 Movies and 178 Shows items were removed for duplicating content already owned locally.

Seeking (dragging the playback position) reliably stalled or hung forever in Proxy mode. FederationStreamHandler.HandleProxyAsync reported Content-Length as rangeStart plus the remote's partial content length, instead of just the partial length - overstating it by exactly the seek offset on every non-zero-start Range request. A client seeking to byte 1,000,000 of a 6,000,000-byte file would be told the response contained 6,000,000 bytes when only 5,000,000 would ever arrive, and would wait indefinitely for the rest. Only the very first Range: bytes=0- request escaped this by coincidence (0 + length == length), which is why playback could start but stalled on every seek and on ordinary buffer-ahead reads. Fixed to report the response's actual partial length; verified live against a real federated stream that Content-Length now matches Content-Range exactly.

A federated item's displayed duration could be wrong forever with no way to recover. Reconciliation restamps an existing item's stream URL in place when it changes (streaming mode, server address, enabled state), but never touched RunTimeTicks - a value stamped once at item creation from whatever the cache held that sync. If that sync ever returned a bad or short value, the item was stuck showing it permanently, even though the cache's own copy gets corrected on every later sync. Reconciliation now compares and restamps RunTimeTicks the same way it already does for the URL, so a wrong duration self-heals on the next sync instead of requiring a full delete/recreate - watch progress is preserved either way.

Also: the federation badge's cloud icon could appear three or four times per card (matched hover-control buttons and footers sharing the same data-id, not just the poster) - now scoped to exactly the card element. The per-item badge and detail-page pill now name which server content is streamed from. Added multi-server pools: one admin creates a named pool and invites servers into it by URL; accepting an invite (still an ordinary friend-request accept - nothing connects without a human clicking Accept) also introduces the new member to every other pool member automatically, so a pool converges into "everyone federates with everyone" without every pair needing a separate manual introduction.

150 tests (up from 133), including new coverage for the cache-supersession fix, the case-insensitive provider id lookup, the Content-Length fix (proved to fail against the pre-fix code), and pool creation/invite/accept-fan-out.

Switching a server off now actually stops its titles playing, and the config page reports whether federation is working. Disabling a server previously only stopped syncing: the dynamic provider refused to serve a source, but Jellyfin independently exposed whatever URL was stamped on the item as a static source, so titles kept streaming from a server the admin had just switched off. Reconciliation now clears that URL - and restores it when the server comes back. Crucially it resolves against every source in priority order rather than just the primary: sources are ordered by priority and never re-ordered by enabled state, so on a deduped title (the same film matched across servers) the preferred server can be off while another still serves it, and keying off the primary alone would have stripped the Play button from an item that was perfectly playable elsewhere - breaking the exact redundancy dedup exists to provide. Toggling the switch now also reconciles immediately instead of leaving the change to take effect up to an hour later on the next scheduled sync. Separately, the page now shows the outcome of the last sync: green when every source refreshed, red with the reason when one did not, plus a note that content from an unreachable server was preserved rather than deleted. Until now that information existed only in the server log, so a library that had quietly stopped updating looked exactly like a healthy one - which is how a switched-off server went unnoticed here for hours. A per-server refresh that throws now records that failure too, instead of leaving the banner showing the previous success. Five tests cover the enabled/disabled source selection, including the deduped-fallback case.

Makes Proxy streaming mode actually take effect on items that already exist, which it never did. Reconciliation only ever created or deleted items - it never updated one - so the stream URL stamped on an item was frozen at the moment it was created. Switching a server to Proxy therefore changed nothing for every title already in the library: Jellyfin still served the stored Direct URL as a static media source *alongside* the freshly built Proxy one, listed it first, and clients played it. That is why switching modes repeatedly appeared to make no difference, and why streaming over a tunnel kept stalling - none of the Proxy relay's retry, idle-timeout and Range-resume handling was ever in the path. Reconciliation now restamps a stale URL in place. Deliberately an in-place update rather than the delete-and-recreate every earlier migration used, because deleting an item discards its watch progress and there is no reason to lose a resume point over a URL change. Verified live: 312 items restamped, after which the item served exactly one media source - the relay - with resume positions intact. Also documents the trap that hid this: Proxy needs the server's own URL, and syncing runs in the background with no incoming request to auto-detect one from, so leaving that field blank silently prevents the relay URL from ever being written. The field's hint now says so.

Usability pass on the config page, driven by a failure that actually happened on this deployment: a remote server had been switched off, and nothing in the UI said so in a way anyone would notice. Its card still showed a name, an address and a full set of settings; the status strip reported "0/1 servers connected" in the same neutral styling as every other number; and step 2 said "No servers available yet", which reads as "you haven't added a server" and sends you off to re-add one you already have. The result was a federated library that had simply stopped working with no visible cause. Now: a banner at the top of the page names every switched-off server and states the consequence, the server's own card is marked with a DISABLED pill and an accent border plus an inline note, the "0/1" turns amber when servers exist but none are live, the checkbox reads "Enabled - sync and play from this server" rather than a bare "Enabled", and step 2 distinguishes "no servers configured" from "all of them are off". Also corrects a genuinely misleading label: the streaming mode picker called Direct "(recommended)" unconditionally and Proxy "slower". Direct hands the player a raw URL to the remote, so nothing retries a dropped read - over the internet, a tunnel or a reverse proxy that is precisely what surfaces as stuttering, while Proxy's resumable relay absorbs it. The two are now labelled "best on a local network" and "best over the internet", each with a line explaining the trade-off.

Fixes a data-loss bug introduced in 0.0.42. That release added a check that a remote is actually running Federation before syncing from it, and deletes a server's entire federated library when it decides the plugin is gone. The check treated *any* unsuccessful probe as "plugin uninstalled" - including a timeout, a refused connection, or a 502/503 from a Cloudflare Tunnel or reverse proxy in front of a briefly-down origin. A tunnel hiccup lasting seconds would therefore have wiped every federated movie and episode from that server, exactly the outcome the surrounding code's own comment claimed it avoided, and a 502 outage of precisely that kind was observed on this setup the same day. The probe is now tri-state: a remote is only treated as having removed the plugin when it 404s this plugin's route *and* separately answers System/Info/Public, proving the address is a live Jellyfin rather than a misrouted tunnel that 404s everything. Anything unverifiable - unreachable, 5xx, or an access gate answering 401/403 - is now an ordinary transient failure that leaves cached content untouched, the same as every other sync failure. Four regression tests pin the specific failure modes (502, unreachable, 404-everything, 403), each verified to fail against the old behaviour. The probe result is also cached briefly per server, so a sync spanning several libraries costs one round trip instead of one per library.

Restores the friend-request system (connect by URL, each side mints an API key for the other automatically on accept, no manual copy-paste) and friends-of-friends discovery, withdrawn in 0.0.27 to stabilize a critical crash fix that shipped in the same release. This is a careful forward-port, not a revert: the withdrawal commit also deleted the plugin subclasses that were crashing every federated item, and 34 releases have touched the same files since (WAN caps, streaming modes, dedup) - reverting outright would have reintroduced that crash and conflicted with everything built since. FederationFriendService, its 8 Friends/* endpoints, the config-page UI, and its full test suite (18 tests) are all back and adapted to today's codebase. Also fixes a real bug found while restoring this: two migration flags (MigratedRemoveShortcutV9, MigratedPlaceholderPathV10) were never added to the config-save endpoint's server-internal-state preservation list, so every settings save from the UI silently reset them - re-triggering a full rebuild of every WAN-capped/shortcut-affected federated item on the next sync after any unrelated change.

Two fixes prompted by a friend's real setup attempt today. (1) Federation only ever talked to a remote's stock Jellyfin API (Items, Users, PlaybackInfo, ...), so nothing about a normal sync actually proved the remote was running Federation itself - it would keep pulling from any reachable Jellyfin server forever, even after Federation was uninstalled there. Every sync now probes the remote's Plugins/Federation/Config route (registered only by this plugin, no API key needed) before pulling its libraries; if a remote no longer answers it, that server's items are actively removed (not just left stale) and nothing new is pulled from it until it reappears - the same removal path DeleteServer already used. (2) The config page's 'Test Server' connection check could report the unhelpful 'Connected but failed to get system info' with no way to tell why: /System/Info/Public (used to confirm reachability) needs no API key, but /System/Info (used right after, for the server name/version) does - so a bad, missing, or under-privileged key looked identical to a dead server. The message now says which: invalid/missing key, insufficient permissions, or the exact HTTP status returned.

Cleans up after itself in two places that previously left dead items behind. (1) Uninstalling the plugin from the dashboard now removes every federated Movie/Series/Season/Episode item it ever created, across every mapped library, before the plugin is unloaded - previously these virtual items (which have no real file behind them) were left in the library forever, since nothing would ever provide a MediaSource for them again or clean them up once the plugin providing that sync was gone. Implemented via BasePlugin.OnUninstalling(), which Jellyfin's plugin manager calls before removing the plugin's own DLL/data folder - that removal step was already handled correctly by Jellyfin core and is unaffected by this change. (2) Confirmed removing a remote server ("Servers/{id}" DELETE) already reconciles every affected library inline and removes its items immediately rather than waiting for the next sync - this was already correct, verified while implementing (1).

Fixes a systemic bug found live while testing 0.0.39: RemoteServerClient's JsonSerializerOptions had no string-enum converter, so System.Text.Json fell back to expecting enum fields as raw numbers instead of names. Every modern Jellyfin server (every remote this plugin talks to) serializes enums as their string name - e.g. "Protocol":"File" - so deserializing any PlaybackInfo response threw on its very first enum field, every single time, for every item, on every server. Confirmed live: querying a remote directly showed an entirely ordinary response, yet the plugin's own deserialization of that exact payload threw JsonException on every attempt. This was not occasional - GetPlaybackInfoAsync has been silently failing on every call and falling back to null, meaning federated items never got the remote's fast, accurate codec/container info and always fell back to local ffprobe discovery instead, and the 15s PlaybackInfo cache added in 0.0.37 never had a successful response to cache. Added JsonStringEnumConverter to the shared JsonOpts. No config or data migration.

0.0.38 fixed the code so newly-created federated items on a WAN-capped Direct-mode server get a working Play button, but reconciliation only ever creates and deletes items - it never updates an existing one in place - so every item already synced before the upgrade was still stuck with the old broken null-Path/Placeholder state. This adds a one-time migration (MigratedPlaceholderPathV10, same mechanism as the V4-V9 migrations before it) that rebuilds every affected existing item on the next sync so it picks up the fix. As with every prior rebuild-based migration in this plugin, item ids are unchanged but local watch progress on rebuilt items is reset - flagged here explicitly since this migration is expected to affect an entire WAN-capped library's worth of items on upgrade, not an edge case.

Fixes a real playback blocker found while testing 0.0.37 live: federated items on a Direct-mode server with WAN bitrate capping enabled (WanCapMode Auto or Manual) had no Play button at all on their own detail page. Root cause: ResolvePlaybackUrl deliberately left item.Path null for those items to avoid freezing a URL that could go stale once the bandwidth classification/measurement changes later. But with Path null, Jellyfin's own static media source comes back as MediaSourceType.Placeholder - literally 'no media here' - and the item-detail endpoint embeds that static source rather than calling this plugin's dynamic provider, so jellyfin-web's Details page saw a Placeholder and never rendered a Play button, regardless of the fully valid, correctly-capped source this plugin's own FederationMediaSourceProvider was already supplying through PlaybackInfo. item.Path is now always stamped (Container set to mp4 to match the forced h264/aac encode when capped, instead of the source file's real container). The staleness this was originally guarding against is already handled elsewhere: when a later bandwidth decision makes the stored Path stale, GetMediaSources already detects the mismatch and serves a corrected alternate source alongside it - worst case a wrong bitrate until that self-heals, not an unplayable item. No config or data migration; existing servers, mappings, and watch progress are untouched.

Two fixes for the most common playback complaints: streaming that glitches/stutters once it starts, and movies that take a long time to start playing. Proxy-mode relaying (Services/FederationStreamHandler) no longer forces a flush after every ~80KB chunk it relays (unnecessary per-chunk overhead that showed up as jitter), gained a 20s idle-read timeout so a stalled remote read fails fast instead of hanging for up to the shared 3-hour HttpClient timeout, and now resumes with a Range request from the last byte actually delivered (up to 2 retries) instead of killing the whole stream on a stall or dropped connection. Separately, FederationMediaSourceProvider was making a live, synchronous, unparallelized remote PlaybackInfo call per federated source on every single play - not just the first - and would re-resolve a fallback admin user via a second remote /Users call every time a server had no UserId configured. Sources are now fetched in parallel (wall-clock bounded by the slowest source, not their sum), PlaybackInfo responses are cached for 15s to absorb rapid repeat requests, and a fallback-resolved user is remembered for the rest of the server session instead of re-queried on every play. No config or data migration; existing servers, mappings, and watch progress are untouched.

Robustness pass on the WAN bandwidth checks added in 0.0.32-0.0.35, prompted by a request to make federation resilient behind things like a Cloudflare Tunnel or any other reverse proxy in front of a remote server. Found a real gap: the bandwidth probe and same-network DNS check had no timeout of their own, inheriting the shared HTTP client's 5-minute timeout - meaning a slow or briefly unresponsive remote (tunnel cold-starting, proxy hiccup, etc.) could stall not just its own check but the entire sync cycle for up to 5 minutes, since this runs at the start of every sync. Both now fail fast on their own short, explicit timeouts (20s for the bandwidth probe, 8s for DNS) instead. Also parallelized these checks across servers - previously sequential, so a mapping with several remote servers multiplied any per-server delay by however many needed rechecking that cycle. None of this changes what topology is supported: the adaptive cap was already transport-agnostic, since it measures real achieved throughput against whatever URL is configured rather than assuming anything about network layout - a tunneled or proxied server already gets classified as not-same-network and measured the same as any other internet-only link. No forced item recreation; existing watch progress and ids are untouched.

Tunes the adaptive WAN bitrate cap added in 0.0.32-0.0.34, per feedback that streaming still wasn't fast/high-bitrate enough: (1) the minimum bitrate the auto-cap will ever request is raised from 4 to 10 Mbps - a connection measuring below that still gets 10 Mbps requested rather than something proportionally lower. (2) The safety margin applied to measured bandwidth is raised from 75% to 85% of what a connection actually measures, so less real, usable bandwidth is left unused. (3) The bandwidth measurement itself now samples 5MB instead of 2MB, reducing how much TCP slow-start (the connection ramping up over its first several round-trips) skews a short sample toward reading lower than the connection's real sustained throughput - most noticeable on faster links. No forced item recreation; existing watch progress and ids are untouched.

Continues 0.0.33's WAN-cap staleness fixes and delete-server cleanup with a redesigned config page. Remote user selection is now a dropdown of the remote server's real accounts (name, admin badge) instead of a blind-pasted GUID, fetched on Test/on demand/once per session for already-connected servers, with a manual-entry fallback if a remote can't be reached. Fixed a real bug in the process: per-field autosave silently swallowed errors, so a failed save gave zero feedback - failures now always surface, successes get a brief 'Saved' confirmation. Per-server connection details now default to open instead of hiding Enabled/User/API key behind a collapsed section, with only the genuinely advanced dials (WAN bitrate cap, image API key) moved into a nested, still-collapsed 'Streaming tuning' section. Also fixed a latent gap where adding a new server didn't send its WAN-cap fields at all (harmless today since they'd just take their defaults, but the same missing-field pattern this plugin has been bitten by before).

Builds on 0.0.31's dedup/badge/resume work with a new adaptive WAN bitrate cap for Direct mode, plus two real bugs found while testing it - still no forced item recreation (existing watch progress and ids are untouched). (1) Direct mode previously always pulled the source's raw, untranscoded file straight from the remote - fine on a local network, but when two servers are only connected over the internet, a 25+ Mbps 4K HDR release can exceed the remote's own upload bandwidth and stutter no matter how fast either machine is. A background check now classifies each server as same-network or internet-only and, only for a confirmed internet link, measures what it can actually sustain (via the remote's own bandwidth-test endpoint, the same mechanism jellyfin-web itself uses) and caps to the largest bitrate that fits - direct play otherwise, always, including the entire time before that first check completes. (2) Found on first real test: item.Path was stamped once, at item-creation time, with whatever that check happened to decide right then - but reconciliation never revisits an existing item, so the decision froze forever even after later classification or a fresh measurement changed what it should now be, so it 'worked for some files, not others' depending purely on when each item was created. A static Path is now only ever stamped when it provably cannot go stale (capping off entirely, or a server positively confirmed same-network) - everything else resolves fresh on every playback request instead. (3) A related bug in that same live path reported the original source's real container/codecs even when actually serving a capped transcode; fixed to report what's actually served. (4) Removing a remote server now cleans up immediately - its items are reconciled out of the library right away instead of lingering until the next sync, and its cached network data is dropped instead of leaking in memory.

0.0.30 stopped new federated items from being created with IsShortcut/ShortcutPath set (which broke playback - see 0.0.30's changelog), but reconciliation only ever creates and deletes items, never updates them in place, so every item already persisted under 0.0.26-0.0.29 kept the stale IsShortcut=true and kept crashing on every playback attempt exactly as before - confirmed directly in a user-supplied log taken after upgrading to 0.0.30. This release adds the missing one-time migration: every existing federated item is rebuilt once more so the stale flag is actually cleared. Local watch progress on federated items is reset, as with prior rebuilds.

Fixes federated movies/episodes getting stuck loading (or silently failing to play at all) on every playback attempt, not just the first. 0.0.26 set IsShortcut/ShortcutPath on federated items to mark their media source IsRemote, believing it was the same mechanism .strm files use - it is not. Jellyfin's ProbeProvider.FetchShortcutInfo unconditionally does File.ReadAllLines(item.Path), expecting Path to point at a real local .strm file whose contents are the target URL; since our Path already *is* that URL, the read throws DirectoryNotFoundException on every metadata refresh. Because that failure prevents MediaStreams from ever being saved, the refresh (and the failure) re-fires on every subsequent playback attempt, and clients observe this as an endless loading spinner, an HLS player left holding a torn-down transcode session (bufferAppendError), or a request that silently gives up. IsShortcut/ShortcutPath are no longer set; Path alone (an http(s) URL) already gives correct LocationType/Protocol without it, and the dynamic per-request media source (FederationMediaSourceProvider) already sets IsRemote independently and is unaffected by this bug.

0.0.28 fixed the 'Cannot deserialize unknown type' reconciliation crash reactively - only once this plugin's own background sync happened to hit it. That left a window, several seconds wide, where any other Jellyfin code path enumerating the same folder first (the web UI, a native library scan, another plugin) could still hit the same crash outside this plugin's control. The purge now runs eagerly at plugin startup, synchronously, before that window opens - so legacy items left over from 0.0.22-0.0.24 are gone before anything else gets a chance to touch them.

Fixes reconciliation still failing after upgrading to 0.0.27. Servers that had run 0.0.22-0.0.24 still had federated items stored in the database under the plugin subclasses removed in 0.0.27 (FederatedMovie, FederatedSeries, ...); Jellyfin can no longer resolve those rows back to a type and throws 'Cannot deserialize unknown type', which aborted the entire folder listing - not just the bad row - so every reconciliation of an affected library failed. Reconciliation now detects this, finds and deletes the unrecoverable rows directly by id (without needing to deserialize them), and retries. Also fixes the 0.0.27 catalog listing itself: its checksum did not match the uploaded release asset, so installing/updating via the plugin catalog failed with a checksum mismatch.

Fixes federated content not appearing at all. 0.0.22 created federated items under plugin subclasses (FederatedMovie, FederatedSeries, ...) so they could override LocationType. Jellyfin resolves an item's kind by parsing the CLR class name into its BaseItemKind enum, so those names threw - and that call sits under both DTO serialization and folder enumeration, meaning every API response containing a federated item returned a 500 and library reconciliation aborted. Items are now created as Jellyfin's own types again; the override is unnecessary because items carry a real remote URL on Path, which already resolves as Remote. Also carries the 0.0.26 streaming fix (items get the remote stream URL on Path so Jellyfin builds a real, probeable HTTP media source instead of an unplayable placeholder). Existing federated items are rebuilt once; watch progress on them is reset. The friend-request and friends-of-friends features are withdrawn for now and preserved on the archive/friend-system branch.

Add opt-in friends-of-friends federation: with the new Allow friends-of-friends setting on, this server asks its friends who their other friends are and automatically sends friend requests to anyone new it discovers (still needs their admin to accept). Off by default. Content stays scoped to what a server actually owns either way - it never re-shares content that was itself federated into it from someone else.

Federated episodes no longer show 'Missing' in the UI. They were materialized as their base Jellyfin CLR types with Path null, so LocationType resolved to Virtual - and the web client paints a 'Missing' badge on any episode with Type == Episode && LocationType == Virtual. Federated items are now created under dedicated subclasses (FederatedEpisode, FederatedMovie, ...) that report LocationType = Remote. One-time rebuild of existing federated items (watch/playback progress on them is reset once).

Fix playback for federated items lacking a configured remote UserId: PlaybackInfo now falls back to the remote's first user automatically (previously it returned null, so media sources carried no Container/MediaStreams and every client reported 'Unable to find a valid media source to play'). Adds logs to confirm stream info is resolved.

Federated seasons and episodes are visible without enabling 'Display missing episodes' (they were stamped IsVirtualItem, which Jellyfin reads as 'missing'). Seasons now carry their IndexNumber, so Jellyfin stops creating a duplicate empty season beside each real one; the duplicates it already created are removed on first sync. Media sources now carry the remote's real container and stream info, without which no client could validate playback. Rebuilds federated Series/Season/Episode items once on upgrade.
Debug logging for the 'unable to find a valid media source' playback error (seasons/episodes are now visible, so this is the next thing to fix). No database changes in this release.

The 0.0.16 fix only recreated Season/Episode items, not the Series itself - a Series never got its own PresentationUniqueKey set, so the match could still fail depending on a library setting. Series are now included in the migration too.

Fix: saving config (from any page load) silently reset the migration-complete flag, since the config page's save payload doesn't include newer fields - causing the whole episode migration to destructively rerun on every config save.

Actual fix for invisible episodes: Jellyfin's show/season pages find children by a SeriesPresentationUniqueKey match, not by parent/ancestor id. Federated episodes never had it set. One-time migration backfills it.
Fix: startup sync and the scheduled sync could run at the same time and corrupt each other mid-migration (SQLite lock errors). Syncs are now serialized, and the migration runs once more cleanly.
One-time migration: recreates existing seasons/episodes so 0.0.13's ordering fix actually applies to them (not just newly-synced ones).
Create shows/seasons/episodes in order (parent before child) so ancestry resolves correctly for browsing.
Fix: seasons were deleted right after being created, so episodes never persisted (no seasons, nothing playable).
Debug logging for the no-seasons/can't-play issue.
TV episodes now sync and play. Fixed duplicate/mismatched-watched-state shows and content looping back in from federated servers.
Actual fix for the missing-movies issue (wrong parent folder).
More debug logging for the missing-movies issue.
Debug logging for the missing-movies issue.

Fix: federated items were saved to the database as orphans, so they never appeared in any library. ILibraryManager.CreateItems does not parent the items it saves - its parent argument only feeds the ItemAdded event - and the plugin never set ParentId itself. The rows therefore matched neither the direct-children query (ParentId) nor the recursive one (AncestorIds, which Jellyfin derives from the ParentId chain at save time), leaving them invisible in the UI and invisible to the plugin's own existence check, which is why every sync re-reported the entire library as newly created. Items are now parented to their provisioned library folder. Item ids are derived deterministically from the cache key, so existing orphaned rows are adopted in place on the next sync - no manual cleanup or database reset needed. Also aligns the repository manifest guid with the plugin's actual id.

Fix: federated items never showed up. Materialized items had Path set to a federation:// URI Jellyfin doesn't recognize, so it treated them as missing/offline everywhere - hidden from browsing and from the plugin's own dedup check, which silently recreated a full duplicate set every hour. Items are now identified by a FederationKey provider id instead, with Path left null (true Virtual item). Upgrading auto-cleans any legacy federation:// duplicates on the next sync, no manual steps needed. Also triggers a background sync 5s after server start so items appear without waiting for the first scheduled task.

Fix: virtual libraries now actually provision. Jellyfin's AddVirtualFolder requires real filesystem paths, so federation:// URIs were rejected. Now uses an empty shadow folder under the plugin data dir; same-name libraries merge into one. Removal only detaches the federation location from merged libraries.
Config page rewrite: sidebar link, guided setup, working buttons, auto-detect public URL. Same-name libraries across servers merge into one. Advanced settings collapsed by default.
many things happened, most of which escaped my gaze
